title: Valcon's custom-build score rose to 5 on an evidenced Appian and Mendix practice with 30+ delivered apps
content:
Valcon's custom-build score was corrected upward from 4 to 5 because evidence appeared for it: Appian held since 2015 via First Technology, Mendix for roughly ten years across 30+ applications including Mendix on SAP, and an explicit business-process-automation practice. The flag calls the low-code practice real and explicit.

That is the opposite kind of correction from the one on Kainos, where a score stayed at 5 and only its evidential status changed. Here the number moved because named partner routes, tenure and delivered application counts were found. Both corrections are recorded in the same field of the same dataset, which is a reminder that a score's history matters as much as its value.

Two things then sit awkwardly together. The flag says Valcon is worth a call, while the row is tiered do-not-pitch; and the recorded revenue of 100 million predates two mergers, so the size input feeding that tier is stale. On the evidence in this row alone, Valcon looks like a candidate for re-tiering rather than a settled exclusion — a deep, self-described automation practice in banking is a nearer neighbour to the pilot's thesis than most rows in this tier.
